miniProject.title: Tiled GEMM to async pipelines with a low-precision error contract
miniProject.brief: Grow kernellab through the GEMM ladder from naive counts to tiled, tensor and pipelined kernels with quantization error and fused epilogues. Every level is gated against a vendor baseline with a held-out fallback. Paths your GPU cannot run, such as Hopper TMA or Blackwell `tcgen05`, are audited statically.
steps: Write a naive overwrite-only GEMM with a shape-to-FLOP calculator and compulsory and requested byte models. Check small products against CPU double precision.

Write shared-memory and register-tiled GEMMs with edge and empty-dimension tests against CPU double products. Add aligned-copy dispatch with scalar tails, compare variants with interleaved trials, keep `cuobjdump -res-usage` reports, and pass LeetGPU challenges 2 and 22.
Draw the tile-ownership diagram and verify one shared-layout permutation with a bank enumerator. Keep the verified permutation in the kernel.

Implement the tensor-core path from MIT 6.S894 Lab 6 `exercise_mma.cu`, pass its numerical tests and inspect the generated MMA instructions. Read Hopper `wgmma` and Blackwell `tcgen05` code, and run it only if your GPU has them.

Implement a two-stage `cp.async` pipeline (compute capability 8.0 or newer) with a stage-lifetime diagram and short-loop and tail regressions. Compare it with the synchronous version using interleaved trials and sanitizer checks.

Decode the low-precision format boundaries and midpoint conversions, separating input-conversion from accumulation error. Compare per-tensor, per-channel and block quantization against an integer-accumulator reference with a predeclared acceptance table.

Add bias and ReLU fusion with a complete-operation timing pair, then compare your ladder against a vendor baseline across a shape matrix. Hold one shape out from tuning for fallback, and report best with losing regimes and residuals.
deliverables: The GEMM ladder with FLOP and byte models, edge tests, sanitizer regressions and resource reports.
The tensor path with instruction evidence, two-stage pipeline with lifetime diagram, and sync against async comparison.
The format decoder with acceptance table, fused epilogue timing pair, and vendor sweep with held-out fallback.

checks.name: LeetGPU GEMM challenges against the reference implementation
checks.note: Run 2 Matrix Multiplication and 22 GEMM in your own harness with matched tolerances; keep shape matrices and losing regimes.

checks.name: MIT 6.S894 Lab 6 tensor-core exercise
checks.note: Build `exercise_mma.cu` with `-arch=native` and keep the supplied fragment and numerical tests.

rubric.pass: Each GEMM level matches the CPU double reference on edge and odd shapes, and the held-out shape passes on fallback.
rubric.strong: Short-loop and tail cases are kept as regressions that fail on the unguarded kernel.

rubric.pass: Thread mapping, stage bytes and resource reports are kept, the lifetime diagram predicts synchronization, and sync against async uses interleaved trials.
rubric.strong: Paths your GPU cannot run are marked as static audit with no performance claim.

rubric.pass: Format boundaries and the input against arithmetic split are tested, quantization states scales and acceptance limits, and the vendor comparison keeps losing regimes.
rubric.strong: Unseen-value saturation is shown, and the fusion saving is derived before the timing pair.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone kernel suite: the GEMM ladder, pipeline and error contract feed attention, Triton and integration. The vendor baseline and dispatch table carry into the final defense.
